content.text: Analysis: The item requires reading a strand diagram with orientation labels, then reasoning about the fork direction. Part A requires determining which template allows continuous 5'→3' synthesis toward the fork. The top template is 5'→3' left to right, so the new strand is antiparallel and runs 3'→5' left to right. Synthesis in the direction of the fork (right) would then require adding nucleotides at the 5' end, which is not possible, so the top template is the lagging template and the bottom template is the leading template. Part B applies that reasoning (5'→3' synthesis only, opposite to fork movement, giving Okazaki fragments). Part C needs complementary pairing and antiparallel orientation: the top template is GATCCTCGC, so the complement is CTAGGAGCG written left to right, with the left end 3' and the right end 5'. This is the main trap, since students often label it 5' on the left. Part D is a standard concept: each daughter duplex has one parental strand and one new strand. The arithmetic load is none, the reading load is low, and the reasoning is moderate, with a single direction-dependent chain of logic and a diagram-to-text representation change. The wording is clear and the content is in scope. This fits a full mock exam.
